A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MedTrinity-25M. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and graphical prompt templates, support reliable comparison. Renamed models and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA experiments with and without MedTrinity-25M pretraining, GPT-4V annotation-alignment evaluations, and dataset analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original VQA results and reports additional model-pretraining comparisons and expert evaluation of generated annotations.

M1.justification: The metadata integration, expert ROI localization, top-eight knowledge retrieval, and hierarchical generation prompt remain substantively unchanged. LLaVA-MedCaptioner/LLaVA-Med++ are renamed LLaVA-Medcap/LLaVA-Tri; LLaMA3 and multiscale feature extraction were already described in v1, including Appendix B. No new algorithmic component is established.

E1.justification: Appendix A retains the same source datasets and sample counts, and evaluation still uses VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and PathVQA. The change from over 90 to over 30 sources and the corrected main-text sample total do not establish changed data coverage; the latter already appeared in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: The SOTA comparator membership in Table 3 is retained. However, v2 Table 4 substantially expands the controlled with/without-pretraining comparison to MiniCPM-V-2.6-8B, InternVL2-8B, and PubMedCLIP. PubMedCLIP previously appeared only as a literature baseline, not in this controlled comparison.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the described 50-sample SLAKE/MIMIC-CXR GPT-4V alignment study with a random 200-sample evaluation using both medical experts and GPT-4V, with scores normalized to 0–1. VQA reporting also introduces average accuracy across open and closed questions. These revise evaluation design and aggregation; three-epoch VQA fine-tuning remains stated.

E4.justification: The pretraining ablation expands from one model to additional MLLMs and a CLIP model, substantially strengthening the investigation of transfer across architectures. The qualitative coarse-caption, ROI, and retrieval ablations remain, while the ROCO comparison example is removed. The added global-context illustration reuses an existing example rather than supplying an independent case.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The larger annotation-evaluation sample and additional evaluator averages change the study design without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Table 4 and replaces dataset-specific alignment scores of 8.2/10 and 8.9/10 with expert and LLM averages of 0.85 and 0.86 under the revised evaluation. LLaVA-Med baseline entries change, including VQA-RAD open/closed scores from 55.5/66.5 to 61.5/84.2, without establishing identical experimental conditions. The proposed model's open/closed VQA scores remain unchanged; its stated PathVQA pretraining gain is corrected from 13.25% to 8.3%.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The data-triplet notation and conceptual hierarchical framework remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central dataset and automated-annotation contributions remain. v2 extends the headline SOTA claim from two benchmarks to all three using the newly displayed averages, highlights benefits across other model families, and revises the source-count claim from over 90 to over 30.

C2.justification: v2 adds a qualification that classification-based open-question baselines may overestimate generalizability and explains how multiple ROIs support global diagnosis. Conversely, deleting Appendix G removes the explicit warning that generated descriptions may remain inaccurate despite metadata and retrieved knowledge. These change qualifications and interpretation within the retained framework.

D1.justification: Deleting v1 Appendix G removes the preprocessing-code link, collection dates, raw-data release policy, intended licensing, and maintenance/access disclosures. The dataset homepage, source tables, expert-model mapping, and prompt templates remain. v2 additionally specifies initial pretraining on 600K PMC-15M image-text pairs; this is newly disclosed detail rather than evidence that the existing training procedure changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting InternVL and MiniCPM-V and removes works including PaLM-E, the ISIC examples, and Datasheets for Datasets. The principal positioning against report-dependent medical datasets and existing medical multimodal models remains. The author–year citation conversion is a presentation change.

P1.justification: There is extensive rewriting of the introduction, related work, data-format explanation, generation description, and dataset-analysis narrative. Section 4 is reorganized into model alignment and broader pretraining evaluation, terminology and model names are revised throughout, and the datasheet section is removed.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the quality table, adds average columns and a separate ablation table, merges the word-count chart into the statistical overview, and redraws the disease word cloud. Several examples move into the appendix, and an existing alignment example is displayed again to explain global context. The ROCO panel and relative-word-count bar chart are removed, although the latter's 3.6% finding remains in prose.

improvement.justification: Expert assessment in Table 2 and broader controlled pretraining experiments in Table 4 strengthen evidence for annotation quality and dataset utility beyond v1's GPT-only quality assessment and single-model ablation. The PathVQA gain correction also improves accuracy. These benefits provide a limited net improvement, tempered by removal of useful datasheet documentation and the annotation-error caveat, together with sparse details about the new expert evaluation.
